rationale: That cluster is film and polymer processing hardware; catalysis is served by the Bayesian-optimisation and flow-chemistry clusters (21 and 15 works).
Film-processing hardware has no biological application path.
Solid and film processing is not solution-phase synthesis.
Molecular synthesis platforms are not battery fabrication; energy materials are served by the SDL cluster.
Organic chemistry is served by two dedicated clusters (23 and 12 works); the apparent hole is where the clustering cut.

Laboratory robotics is biologically concentrated (26 biomolecule works) and has zero battery or energy work, even though batteries are the single best-served domain for autonomous platforms (41 works in the thin-film/polymer SDL cluster).
Same boundary in the other direction.
The mobile robotic-chemist and acceleration-platform lineage has no battery work at all, despite batteries being the densest application domain for closed-loop platforms.
Bayesian reaction optimisation is well developed but partitions into the flow-chemistry cluster.
Quantum and photonic materials are the sparsest domain in the corpus (42 of 1,923 works) and high-throughput screening, the obvious first approach, barely touches them.
Same pattern: no robotics-tradition automation addresses device-grade thin films.
1279 of 1923 works (66.5%) name no specific material class. Growth is methodological and agentic rather than material-specific.
Lowest closed-loop shares in the corpus (0.368 and 0.435) against 0.696 for thin films. Automation without loop closure is the modal state where the assay is slow or destructive.
